before: A digitally controlled USB-C laboratory supply was developed from a charge-pump PFC resonant converter and supplied planar magnetics. The first prototype, V1, was used for circuit bring-up and control development. V2 integrated the MCU and associated circuitry on the converter PCB. The V3 edge-card layout was then developed to reduce the converter volume.
after: The work started with a DTU charge-pump converter and supplied planar magnetics. The hardware and controller were then built around these parts for a USB-C power supply. The main change was the load: it could be absent at startup, draw different amounts of power, or be disconnected while the converter still held energy. That change connects the circuit design, burst-control development, and tests described in this thesis.
